transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, what brings me in is that I just feel like I'm constantly running on a motor lately. Like, I'll finish one thing at school—I'm a special education teacher, by the way, been doing it for years. I actually had this one kid, Tommy, just the sweetest boy but he would always try to eat the crayons, especially the blue ones, no idea why. Anyway, I finish one thing at school or at home, and I immediately jump into the next thing without ever being able to shut myself off. It's exhausting, but I just can't stop. I bought a new lawnmower last weekend, thinking maybe yard work would help burn it off, but I ended up mowing my neighbor's lawn too because I just couldn't sit down.
During this time, how has your sleep been?

Sleep? Um, I haven't really noticed anything different, honestly. I just kind of keep going until I crash. My wife did just buy us one of those new mattresses, though. You know, the ones that come vacuum-sealed in a box? It is just wild how they fit a whole king-size bed into a cardboard box. The delivery guy—poor kid, he looked like he was maybe 19, tops—was just sweating bullets trying to get it up our front steps. I actually ran out and helped him carry it, and then I gave him a Gatorade from the garage fridge. Lemon-lime, obviously, because that's the only good flavor. My daughter drinks the blue ones, which always reminds me of Tommy and the blue crayons, but... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, I don't know, I guess I haven't really paid attention to it. It seems fine?
Have you struggled with feeling driven by a motor like this since you were a child, or did it start recently?

Oh, gosh, no, this isn't new at all. It's not something that just started with this family change recently, it's been my whole life. My mother used to joke that even back in elementary school, I was basically teaching the class from my seat. Well, I say "from my seat," but I was really always out of my chair, talking to everyone, or cutting in before the teacher even finished giving the directions. 

Which, being a teacher myself now, I completely understand how frustrating that is! But those old desks, you know, the ones where the wooden chair is attached to the desk with that thick metal pipe? I actually got my knee stuck between the pipe and the wood in the third grade because I was twisting around so much. The janitor—Mr. Abernathy, I think his name was—had to come up with a wrench to take the whole desk apart to get me out. He always smelled like peppermint and floor wax. I actually keep a bowl of peppermints on my desk now for my students because of him. Though I have to keep a close eye on them so they don't swallow them whole, or try to color with them, like Tommy. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. Yeah, this motor thing. It was part of who I was long before adulthood. It’s always been there.
Aside from feeling constantly on the go, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or details that require your sustained attention?

Focus? Um, I don't... I don't really think so? I mean, I can focus just fine when I need to. Like when I'm working with my students, I'm right there with them. We were doing this project on the solar system last week, and I spent hours cutting out these little foam planets. Foam is such a weird material, isn't it? It squeaks when you cut it with scissors. It's the exact same sound as when you rub two pickles together. Have you ever done that? My uncle showed me that trick at a family barbecue when I was maybe ten. He worked at a deli, so he always had these massive barrels of pickles. The garlic ones were the best. He used to say the secret was putting a whole clove of garlic in the jar, not just the minced stuff. I tried it once, but my wife said the fridge smelled like an Italian restaurant for a month. We ended up having to buy all these baking soda boxes to absorb the smell. You know, they say you're supposed to change those out every thirty days, but who actually remembers to do that? I usually just wait until the milk starts tasting funny. But, um... what were we talking about? Details? No, I don't think I have a problem with that. I'm pretty good at paying attention to things.
Do you frequently misplace or have trouble keeping track of items you need every day, like your keys, wallet, or phone?

Keys and wallet? No, I don't think so. I actually have this little leather tray right by the front door where I put everything the second I walk in. My daughter bought it for me for Father's Day a few years ago. She got it custom stamped with my initials, but the guy at the craft fair accidentally stamped 'J.R.' instead of 'J.B.' I didn't have the heart to tell her, so I just use it anyway. 

Craft fairs are getting so ridiculously expensive now, aren't they? We went to one last autumn, and this guy was selling wooden spatulas for like forty dollars. Who pays forty dollars for a spatula? I mean, I love to cook, especially making pancakes on Saturday mornings, but a cheap plastic one flips a flapjack just as well. I usually put blueberries in mine. My students always tell me I should bring some in for them, but with all the food allergies these days, you can't just bring home-baked goods into a classroom anymore. It's a shame, really. When I was a kid, people brought in cupcakes for every birthday. The ones with the thick grocery-store frosting that stained your teeth blue for the rest of the day... 

Um, wait. Did you ask about my phone? Or my wallet? Yeah, no, I don't really lose my stuff. I always know where it is.
